en: The Brief Ritual for Homa from the *Mañjuśrī-samaya-darśana-mukha-mahātantrarāja*,
translated during the Song Dynasty by the State Preceptor of the Great Qidan (Liao) Empire, the Master from Magadha in Central India.
I take refuge in all Buddhas and the assembly of great Bodhisattvas.
Now I shall explain the various rituals for homa;
first, one should recite the mantra to empower the spade and pickaxe.
Thereafter, one should provide a detailed analysis.
The mantra for empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) is: Oṃ ni-kha-na va-su-de-svāhā. Reciting this mantra, one empowers the spade and pickaxe.
Dig the homa hearth.
Before digging the hearth, first take river water and place it in a clean vessel;
empower it by reciting the mantra of the Buddha of the respective family.
Sprinkle water upon the ground, the clean spade and pickaxe, and the person who digs the hearth.
The mantra for sprinkling purification is: Oṃ amṛtodbhava hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. If one follows the homa ritual:
One night before digging the hearth,
empower *jīva-bali* (living-rice) with the mantra of the Vidyārāja of the Upper Direction,
and offer it to the local deities (*sthānapati*) and the eight classes of gods and nāgas.
However, one may dig a hearth;
the soil from within that hearth should be collected in a clean place,
and then sand should be taken from within a river.
First, empower the sand with the mantra.
The mantra is: Oṃ vāsudhātryai vāsushriye oṃ. Having recited this mantra, perform the empowerment.
Fill the interior of the furnace with sand;
next, rub its surface with the powder of the five precious stones, the seven jewels, and the four metals,
before one may then use the pure bricks.
When constructing the homa hearth, do not use bricks.
First, recite the Vajrakarmabodhisattva mantra.
The mantra for consecrating the purified bricks is as follows:
Oṃ vajrakarma khaṃ. Having performed the consecration in this manner, one should construct it using purified bricks according to the ritual rules.
Regarding the *homa* ritual, four types are taught. These four types are: first, *śānti*, which means "pacification";

second, *puṣṭi*, which is translated as "augmentation" or "prosperity"; third, *vaśa*, which is translated as "subjugation through love"; and fourth, *āveśa*, which is translated as "subjugation. There are likewise four types of *homa* hearths corresponding to these four.
Regarding these four types:
if one seeks *santi* (pacification), one should construct a circular hearth;
if one seeks *puṣṭi* (prosperity), one should construct a hearth shaped like a half-moon or an octagon.
If seeking *vaśya*, the hearth (*kuṇḍa*) should be made four-cornered;
if seeking *āveśa*, it should be made three-cornered.
These four types should be constructed according to what is appropriate.
Next, the measurements of the homa hearth are explained.
Briefly, there are three types.
First, the hearth for offerings is eight cubits [in size].
This is an octagonal hearth,
measuring two cubits in depth.
The second offering hearth measures one and a half cubits.
The depth is one and a half cubits;
the four sides together are six cubits;
the third, the offering hearth, is one cubit.
The four sides are each four cubits [in length], and the depth is likewise one cubit.
Construct three tiers of rims according to the size of the hearth.
On the third rim, on the western side of the front of the hearth.
The measurement is half that of the main structure.
It is also constructed using clean bricks, forming nine tiers that gradually diminish toward the top.
To the right of the main structure, a series of stepped terraces is built.
The left half is built straight up and down;
the three tiers of the hearth’s rim represent the three realms,
and its nine levels represent the nine stages (bhūmis).
Having performed this, one should place the bricks upon the sand inside the furnace.
One should gather the seven jewels, the four types of iron filings, and the five grains,
visualizing them as being composed of the five seed-syllables and the seven jewels and four metals.

The seven treasures are gold, silver, pearl, crystal, beryl, lapis lazuli, and amber. The four metals are gold, silver, copper, and iron. The five grains are rice, non-glutinous rice, wheat, mung beans, and sesame. These [are mixed with] the powder of the five grains and the four metals.
Recite the mantra of Vairocana to perform empowerment. The mantra is:
Oṃ vajradhātu vaṃ. Having recited this mantra, next recite the mantras of the four Bodhisattvas of the Pāramitās.
Empower the powder of the seven jewels with this mantra: Vajrapāramitā Bodhisattva.
Oṃ sattvavajri hūṃ. Bodhisattva Ratnapāramitā. Oṃ ratnavajri traḥ. Bodhisattva Dharmapāramitā.
Oṃ dharmavajri hrīḥ, Karmapāramitā Bodhisattva. Oṃ karmavajri aḥ.
Having thus recited this mantra and performed the empowerment, ... [the ritual continues] ...
Use it to collect [the materials] within the furnace.
One should mix all types of powdered incense with the clay.
The mantra for consecrating the clay is as follows:
Oṃ vāsudhāre śrīye śrīvāsudeva svāhā. Having recited this mantra, [one should proceed].
One should smear the hearth with fragrant clay.
Having completed the arrangement according to the sequence above,
one should clearly visualize the maṇḍala within the hearth and settle the mind upon its layout.
When performing the *śānti* rite, one should visualize the body of the Buddha as white in color.
One should further contemplate that the appearance of one's own body is likewise so.
With the left hand, one should hold the rosary by pressing upon the second joint of the ring finger.
Make offerings by burning incense.
Using one hundred and eight crystal rosary beads,
sit facing east and perform the two-fold union of the *puṣṭi* rite.
Visualize the Buddha as golden in color, and imagine yourself likewise.
Within the intervals of the vows (*praṇidhāna-pāramitā*), count by snapping the fingers;
use one hundred *bodhi* seeds for the beads.
Sit facing south.
Perform the *vaśa* rite.
Visualize the Buddha as vermilion-yellow in color, and likewise visualize yourself as such.
Within the square boundary and inside the circle, hold the prayer beads;
use ninety lotus seeds; sit facing west.
Perform the *avīcāra* rite;
visualize the Buddha as green, and likewise visualize yourself as such.
Hold the rosary upon the first joint of the index finger.
Using seventy *śrīphala* seeds, sit facing north.
When performing the homa rite for any of the four types of desired objectives at any time,
one should visualize the respective mandalas within the hearth.
One should place [the deity] in the center, visualizing them as the presiding lord of the specific ritual section being performed.
If this is outside of the four types of homa rituals,
it should be done as a regular daily offering.
One should visualize Akṣobhya Buddha in the center.
The rosary should consist of one hundred and eight beads, or an indefinite number as required.
Regarding the method for visualizing the maṇḍala upon it, it is as extensively explained in the Great Teaching (Mahātantra).
Having performed such visualization, one should take *śakrābhilagna* grass;
if unavailable, one should substitute it with fine, soft, green, and exquisite grass. It should be used to form eight knots and placed at the eight directions of the hearth.
One symbolizes the eight stages of pure perception.
Furthermore, one uses three knots of *kuśa* grass and arranges them within the hearth to symbolize the positions of the Three Jewels.
Moreover, one ties three *maṅgala-kuśa* blades together into a single knot.
The three bonds together with the nine fetters constitute the homa ritual;
first, one burns [the offerings] to represent the purification of the hearth,
and further uses two knots of grass.
Tie one knot and place it inside the consecration flask;
tie another knot and place it upon the ring finger of the right hand,
visualizing it as a *homa* mallet.
Furthermore, the hand of purity is represented as Vajrapāṇi;
the grass-knot is in the shape of a vajra.
One should empower it with the four wisdom mantras, which are as follows:

Oṃ sidhalocanī sarvārthasādhani svāhā. Oṃ kili kili mama kṛte sarvārthasādhani svāhā. Oṃ śvete pannaravāsini jayanti sarvārthasādhani svāhā. Oṃ tṛ tṛtṛ tṛ hūṃ svāhā. Having thus performed the consecration:
One should take firewood that has been properly dried according to the rules;
it may be considered equivalent to the donor.
Measure one cubit with the hand,
sprinkle it with scented water,
and recite the Vairocana mantra.
The mantra for empowerment is:
Oṃ vajradhātu vaṃ. Having performed the empowerment through this ritual, place the fuel within the hearth.
The roots and tips should be used according to their natural state;
however, if they are thorny wood,
they must not be used within the ritual.
Having performed the arrangement as described above,
one should consecrate the homa fuel sticks with mantras,
also reciting the Vairocana-vidyā.
And he empowers it with mantras.
In Sanskrit, this is called *pañca-sāleya-rasmi*, which means "five-milk wood"; it represents the offering-rice of the five Tathāgatas' true lineage.
Regarding the five types of milky wood used:
these refer to trees such as the nyagrodha and others.
Since these are not available in this region, one should simply take wood that does not shed its leaves and is without fruit.
Make the branches slender;
dip the tips of the roots in clarified butter.
Use three sticks or five branches.
Alternatively, one may offer twenty-five twigs into the fire,
visualizing that they are being presented as an offering to the Buddha.
One should use five kinds of grain,
perform the rite of burnt offerings,
and recite the mantra of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāramitā.
First, consecrate the five grains. The mantra is:
Oṃ sattvavajri hūṃ. Having thus consecrated the five grains.
Offer them in successive order.
To symbolize the roots of this food, offer ghee, honey, milk, curd,
and so forth, while also reciting the Vajrapāramitā mantra.
First, perform the consecration (*adhiṣṭhāna*).
Next, offer worship by performing *homā* with five kinds of gruel.
The five gruels are those made of milk, curd, clarified butter (*ghṛta*), honey, sugar-cane juice, and granulated sugar.
The mantra for empowering the Bodhisattva Dharmapāramitā through mindfulness is as follows:
Oṃ dharmavajri hīḥ. Having thus empowered it, [one should proceed].
This constitutes a pure offering.
One should empower five types of rice and five kinds of gruel using the root *pāramitā* mantra. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ śaṅkari śāntikari kṣutaṇi ghaṭaya sarvarthasādhani svāhā. Having thus empowered the five kinds of food, [one should offer them].
The ritual for manifesting the dharma is also the same as before.
Having completed the empowerment according to the ritual as described above,
one should visualize a Vidyārāja upon the hearth.
Visualize one's own body as a śarīra stūpa,
and further imagine that all Buddhas are within the stūpa;
perform the homa and offer mental worship.
However, one may take fire. Regarding the visualization of that fire, it corresponds to the specific rite being performed;
the seed-syllable of the Lord of the Family (Kulapati) serves as the fire.
Alternatively, one may empower [the object] with the root mantra;
or internally visualize the fire of wisdom emitting great flames;
or visualize the fire-flames pervading the body of the Vidyārāja.
Transform the materials to be burned into an offering.
Once the fire has been kindled,
purify it by sprinkling it with pure water and fragrant unguents.
Next, below the water surface, one should prepare pure water;
then use ghee, honey, milk, and curd,
as well as the five kinds of firewood, the five kinds of grain porridge, and cooked rice.
First, cast five [offerings] into the fire for each [deity],
making individual offerings to the five Tathāgatas while reciting the respective root-mantras (mūlavidyā) of those Tathāgatas.
The mantras for making offerings by burning substances to the five Tathāgatas are as follows:

Vairocana Tathāgata: Oṃ vajradhātu vaṃ. Akṣobhya Tathāgata: Oṃ akṣobhya hūṃ. Ratnasambhava Tathāgata: Oṃ ratna svabhāva traḥ. Amitābha Tathāgata: Oṃ amitābha hrīḥ. Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata: Oṃ amoghasiddhi aḥ. Having first visualized the offering to these five Buddhas, [one proceeds].
Next, offer water for rinsing the mouth.
Visualize that it is given to the Buddha to rinse his mouth.
The mantra for offering the water is as follows:
Oṃ kṛluṇade hūṃ kṛrumukaga oṃ. Having thus made an offering with flowers, cast them into the fire pit.
Visualize a flower upon the crown of the Buddha’s head; this is the mantra for offering flowers.
*Oṃ sarvatathāgata puṣpa pūjā*. Then, using scented unguent, offer it and sprinkle it into the fire.
Visualize that one is anointing and sprinkling all the Buddhas.
The mantra for offering incense is:
Oṃ sarvatathāgata-gandha-pūjā. Furthermore, offer incense with this mantra.
Visualize the incense entering the Buddha’s nostrils as an offering to all Tathāgatas.
The mantra for the offering of burning incense is:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatadhūpapūjāye svāhā. Ring the bell while reciting this or chanting verses at all appropriate times.
Next, burn the five grains while recollecting the object of one's aspiration;
empower the substances with the mantra of the Lord of the Family before burning them.
If there is no other specific object to be sought,
one should merely recite the *dhāraṇī* of the Dharma-relics while burning offerings.
The offering mantra is as follows:
Oṃ dharmadhātu-garve svāhā. Having burned the five grains, one should then offer three portions each of ghee, honey, milk, and curd into the fire.
Next, one should cast water into the vessel while performing the visualization and making offerings according to the previous ritual method.
Next, offer congee; first burn milk congee, and thereafter burn other types of congee as desired.
When boiling the congee,
take eight pure vessels,
or take eight lotus petals and sprinkle them with scented unguents.
Place the gruel and rice in a clean vessel and empower it with the mantras of the deities of the ten directions;
offer it at the eight corners of the hearth to the deities of the ten directions, including the two directions above and below.
One should visualize making offerings to the deities of the ten directions.
The sequence of the vidyās shall now be explained.
The mantra of Śakra, the Deva of the East, is as follows:
Namo samanta-buddhānām indrāya svāhā. This is the mantra of the Fire Deity of the southeast.
Namo samanta-buddhānām. Akṣaye svāhā. This is the mantra of Yama-deva of the southern direction.
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ* (1) *yamāya svāhā* (2). This is the mantra of the celestial lord of the rākṣasas in the southwest.
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ* (1) *mṛgaśanāya svāhā* (2). This is the mantra of the water deity in the west.
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ vāruṇāya svāhā.* This is the mantra of Vāruṇa, the Devaputra of the northwest. *Namo samantabuddhānāṃ vāyave svāhā.* This is the mantra of Vāyu, the Devaputra of the northwest.
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ vaiśravaṇāya svāhā.* This is the mantra of Vaiśravaṇa, the Devaputra of the north.
Namo samantabuddhānāṃ. Vaiśravaṇāya svāhā. The mantra of Īśāna, the deity of the northeast, is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām* (1) *īśānāya svāhā* (2). This is the mantra of Brahmā, the True Deity of the upper direction.
*Namo samantabuddhānām* (1) *brahmaṇe svāhā* (2). This is the mantra of the Earth Deity of the lower direction.
Namo samanta-buddhānām | Pṛthivīye svāhā | Svāhā | These are the deities of the ten directions.
First, one should establish eight seats in the eight directions around the hearth for Brahmā,
the Earth Deity, and the others.
Visualize [the fire] above and below the hearth,
then pour the water from within the vessel into the food being offered.
Next, use incense and flowers for anointment;
offer the incense according to the respective positions.
Each person should recite their own root mantra to consecrate the offering substances.
Recite the root mantra three times and install it in its original position.
Then, one may offer a burnt rice porridge (caru). Once the burnt rice porridge has been offered:
Ghee, honey, milk, and curd—
each of these three is cast into the fire;
water is added next, following the same sequence as the previous method.
Next, one should offer the rice as an oblation; first burn the milk-rice, then the ghee-rice, and finally the curd-rice.
Having thus burned the rice, [proceed].
Ghee, honey, milk, and curd—
each of these three substances is cast into the fire;
the subsequent addition of water follows the same procedure as before.
Furthermore, take the tips and roots of the homa fuel sticks,
dip them in clarified butter (ghṛta), and cast them into the fire;
likewise, use clarified butter, honey, milk, and curd.
Offer three oblations of each into the fire in this sequence; when it is finished, stand up,
holding the vessel of clarified butter along with the *sruva* ladle.
Ring the bell while reciting the mantra;
offer clarified butter into the fire.
All those who rejoice [in this]—
Each person shall smear their hands with [fragrant substances], hold flowers, and wait for the recitation and praise until the pouring of the clarified butter is complete.
Then, each shall cast a flower into the fire-pit and proceed to the fire altar to perform prostrations, thereby manifesting the perfection of the offering.
Next, use a clean cloth to wipe [the vessel] and cover the fire with clarified butter while burning it.
Visualize this as the Buddha’s robe; once this is completed, one should use a pure flask to pour water around the furnace.
Furthermore, one should rinse the mouth and perform the purification ritual. When performing homa,
one should apply focused visualization with a sincere mind.
There is no need for haste in making offerings.
The materials to be offered should be about the size of an *āmra* fruit— here in this land, roughly the size of an apricot— as described for the homa altar.
One should know that among all forms of offering, the tongues of the seven Buddhas and the mouths of billions of devas are supreme.
Homa is the most supreme; whatever five-grain porridges,
cooked rice, and so forth are not completely consumed by the fire [should be offered].
Furthermore, take other foods and drinks,
as well as various flowers and fruits,
and place them all together in a single vessel.
Sprinkle it with scented ointment and fumigate it with incense.
First, perform the mudrā of summoning.
Perform the Samaya-lotus and Vajra-bond mudrās; next,
dipping [the bell] halfway into the water, ring it while reciting the mantra for consecrating the food.
Visualize making offerings to the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas, as well as all the deities outside the fire altar;
direct the mind to make offerings to them all.
Having thus performed the homa offering:
Thereafter, I dedicate the secret and sublime merit thus accumulated to all the noble assemblies,
so that it may universally benefit all sentient beings.
A Brief Ritual for Homa from the King of Great Teachings, the Sūtra on the Gate of Mañjuśrī’s Equal Contemplation.
